**define** a nonzero causal vector $v\in T_pM$ to be **future-directed** when
$g_p(v,N_p)<0$ and **past-directed** when $g_p(v,N_p)>0$. The classification of
nonzero causal vectors into exactly these two classes, and its agreement with
the two components of the timelike set (the future component is the component
$C_p^+$ containing $N_p$, and the future closed null cone is
$\operatorname{cl}(C_p^+)\setminus\{0\}$), is proved in
[[lem-gr-future-causal-classification-by-a-timelike-field]]; in particular no
nonzero causal $v$ satisfies $g_p(v,N_p)=0$, so the definition is exhaustive and
mutually exclusive. Replacing $N$ by $-N$ reverses every future/past label, and
two time orientations $N,N'$ determine the same future-directed causal vectors
at every point where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)<0$, while they determine opposite ones
where $g_p(N_p,N'_p)>0$, by
[[lem-gr-timelike-fields-define-equal-or-opposite-future-cones]]; that lemma
also shows the sign of $p\mapsto g_p(N_p,N'_p)$ is constant on every connected
component of $M$.

**(d) The inverse metric.** Because $g_p$ is nondegenerate, it induces at each
$p$ an isomorphism $\flat_p:T_pM\to T_p^*M$, $v\mapsto g_p(v,\cdot)$, and an
inverse metric $g_p^{-1}$ on the dual space; the inverse metric, the musical
isomorphisms and the components $g^{ab}$ are defined separately on this page,
where the smoothness of those components is also proved. Neither construction
uses any choice principle beyond the one already recorded in (c).

**Convention and scope.** The physical reading of a smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold as a classical spacetime model, and the domain in which
that reading is adopted, are recorded in the framework postulate
`post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain`; the words spacetime and event carry no
mathematical content beyond this definition, and this item asserts no claim
about nature. The dimension $4$ and the absence of boundary are part of the
data; nothing in the definition assumes that $M$ is nonempty or connected, and
no completeness, extendibility or maximality property of $(M,g)$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: (Jacobi fields are linear in the parallel transport.) Fix $v\in W$ and let $P_t:T_pM\to T_{\gamma_v(t)}M$ be the parallel transport along $\gamma_v$ from $0$ to $t$ for $t\in[0,1]$; by [L3], $P_t$ is a linear isometry and $t\mapsto P_tX$ is the unique parallel field along $\gamma_v$ with value $X$ at $t=0$. Since $\gamma_v([0,1])\subseteq\exp_p(W)=U$ by star-shapedness, $R(\gamma_v(t),\cdot)\gamma_v(t)=0$ for every $t$, so $D_t^2J=0$ is the Jacobi equation of [L3]. The field $J(t):=tP_tX$ satisfies $J(0)=0$, $D_tJ=P_tX$ (because $D_t(P_tX)=0$ and $D_t(tP_tX)=P_tX$), hence $D_t^2J=0$ and $D_tJ(0)=X$. By uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data, $J_X(t)=tP_tX$.

(Converse direction.) Suppose a chart $(V,y)$ has constant components $g_{ab}=\eta_{ab}$. Then all $\partial_cg_{ab}$ vanish, and [L4] gives $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$ and $R^a{}_{bcd}=0$ on $V$; since the curvature is a tensor and its components vanish in one chart, $R\equiv0$ on $V$. This proves (e).

(The differential of the exponential map is an isometry.) Fix $v\in W$ and $X,Y\in T_pM$. By [L2] and step 1.1, $d(\exp_p)_v(X)=J_X(1)=P_1X$ and likewise $d(\exp_p)_v(Y)=P_1Y$. The map $d(\exp_p)_v$ is linear because it is a differential, and by the isometry property of $P_1$ in [L3], $$g_{\exp_p(v)}\bigl(d(\exp_p)_vX,d(\exp_p)_vY\bigr)=g_{\exp_p(v)}(P_1X,P_1Y)=g_p(X,Y).$$ Hence $d(\exp_p)_v$ is a linear isometry. This proves (a).

(The exponential map is a local isometry.) By [L1] the map $\exp_p|_W:W\to U$ is a diffeomorphism onto $U$, and by step 2.1 its differential at every $v\in W$ is a linear isometry; by [L5] this means $(\exp_p)^*g=g_p$ on $W$, that is, $\exp_p$ is an isometry of $(W,g_p)$ onto $(U,g)$. This proves (b).

(Constant components in the exponential chart.) Let $u=\psi\circ\exp_p^{-1}$ be the exponential chart and $\partial_a^u$ the corresponding coordinate fields; by [L5] applied to the diffeomorphism $\exp_p$ and the definition $e_a=\psi^{-1}$-image of the standard basis, $$g_{ab}(q)=(\exp_p^*g)_{u(q)}\bigl(e_a,e_b\bigr)=g_p(e_a,e_b)=\eta_{ab}\qquad(q\in U).$$ Thus all components of $g$ in the chart $u$ equal the constants $\eta_{ab}$, proving (c) and the displayed formula of the statement; in particular the chart $u$ is an isometry of $U$ onto the open set $u(U)\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ carrying the Minkowski form.

(Open flat sets and conclusion.) Let $p\in O$ with $R\equiv0$ on the open set $O$. Since $\exp_p$ is continuous with $\exp_p(0)=p$ and $O$ is open, there is $\delta>0$ with $\exp_p(B_\delta(0)\cap\mathcal E_p)\subseteq O$; the set $W_0:=B_\delta(0)\cap\mathcal E_p$ is open and star-shaped about $0$ (an intersection of star-shaped sets), and after shrinking $\delta$ so that $\exp_p$ is a diffeomorphism on $W_0$ the hypotheses of the theorem hold with $W_0$ in place of $W$, so conclusions (a)-(c) hold for $W_0$; this proves (d) for the point $p$, and applying the same construction at each $q\in O$ gives each point of $O$ a neighborhood isometric to an open subset of Minkowski space. Together with step 1.2 this proves (d) and (e), and steps 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 prove (a), (b) and (c) under the stated hypothesis.

boundaries.reason: The neighborhood W is a nonempty star-shaped open set and U = exp_p(W); no empty family or sum occurs.

boundaries.evidence: step 5.1 uses exp_p(0) = p and takes W₀ contained in the exponential domain near the zero vector, disposing of the zero-vector case of the normal neighborhood.

boundaries.reason: The dimension is four and the orthonormal basis has four elements; no one-dimensional case is claimed.

boundaries.evidence: the statement assumes R ≡ 0 on U and W star-shaped inside the exponential domain, excluding the degenerate cases in which exp_p fails to be a diffeomorphism; step 3.1 uses the diffeomorphism property explicitly.

step 1.1 evaluates the Jacobi fields at t ∈ [0,1], including the endpoint t = 1 where d(exp_p)_v(X) = J_X(1), and step 5.1 restricts to an open W₀ whose image lies in O, covering the endpoint value v = 0 of the exponential map.

boundaries.reason: The point p, the star-shaped neighborhood W and the orthonormal basis (e_0,...,e_3) are fixed data.

boundaries.evidence: steps 1.1-4.1 prove the forward direction: R ≡ 0 on U makes exp_p a local isometry with constant components η_ab in the exponential chart.
step 1.2 proves the converse direction: a chart with constant components η_ab forces Γ ≡ 0 and R ≡ 0 on its domain, completing clause (e).

citations.quote:
Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework the
following statements.

**(i) Spacetime model.** The spacetime of a model of the framework is a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ as in
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: a smooth four-manifold $M$ without
boundary, a Lorentzian metric $g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and a time orientation $N$. Its points represent
idealized physical events; the vector $N$ fixes which causal directions are
future-directed; and the causal classification of tangent vectors along any
worldline is the classification of the Lorentz vector spaces $(T_pM,g_p)$
together with the future/past convention of the time orientation. The metric
$g$ is the gravitational field of the model: it is the object that the field
law of the framework constrains, and its curvature is the model's
representation of gravity. The rules by which ideal clocks, test bodies and
light rays couple to $g$ are adopted separately as physical assumptions of the
framework.

**(ii) Classical domain.** Geometry and matter are treated as classical
continuum fields: the model describes macroscopic configurations of matter and
a classical metric, with no quantum description of either. The framework makes
no claim that a real spacetime is exactly such a manifold, that matter is
exactly a classical continuum, or that the smooth description applies to
arbitrarily small scales or arbitrarily strong fields; those are domain
limitations of the model family, not consequences of it.

**(iii) Unity of the model.** A model of the framework is specified by its
geometry $(M,g,N)$ together with its matter content and the field law adopted
for it; the geometry alone selects no matter configuration and no dynamics
(the matter assumptions are
adopted separately, in the companion postulate on matter content). Physical
parameters enter through
the unit conventions of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no
numerical value of a constant is asserted here.

**(iv) Smooth-branch restriction.** The fields of a model are defined on an
open domain of $M$; the metric is $C^\infty$ on all of $M$ and $M$ has no
boundary. Configurations in which a field fails to be smooth on a nonempty open
set, in which matter is concentrated on a lower-dimensional set in a way that
produces a distributional stress-energy tensor, or in which $M$ carries a
boundary, are outside the stated smooth domain of the framework and require
mathematics not supplied by these postulates.

**(v) Status.** These are adopted assumptions. They are not derived from the
mathematics of manifolds, from any symmetry principle, or from experiment; the
equivalence principle and covariance arguments motivate but do not prove them.
Testing the framework means comparing predictions computed from a fully
specified model — geometry, matter content and field law — with observations,
and agreement is evidence about the model, not a proof of these postulates.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]], the following statements
about the matter content of a model.

**(i) Matter content is model input.** A model of the framework specifies its
nongravitational fields or matter and their explicit equations of motion and
couplings. The geometric data $(M,g,N)$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and covariance of the model's equations
under relabelling of events do not select those fields, equations or couplings:
different matter specifications over the same geometry are different models of
the framework, and no dynamical selection principle is asserted.

**(ii) Smooth matter and its stress-energy tensor.** The matter of a model on
its matter domain is represented by smooth fields on an open domain
$U\subseteq M$, and the model's stress-energy tensor is the smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field $T$ on $U$ of
[[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]], with the unit reading recorded there.
The relation of $T$ to the matter fields is part of the model: a model derived
from an action defines $T$ as the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of that action,
while a model that prescribes $T$ directly is a separate source model.

**(iii) Consistency with the field law.** Where a model prescribes $T$
independently of matter fields, the prescription is admissible only if it meets
the consistency conditions imposed by the gravitational field law adopted for
the model, stated where that law is stated; in the action formulation the
matter equations, their coupling to the metric, and the on-shell conservation
of $T$ are derived within the model rather than assumed. Conservation is an
on-shell statement about a specified model and is not automatic for an
arbitrary smooth symmetric $T$.

**(iv) Energy conditions are optional additional assumptions.** A model may
adopt any of the pointwise inequalities of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] as
further assumptions on its stress-energy tensor. None of them is a consequence
of the preceding clauses, of the field law, or of the symmetry of $T$; each
model records which conditions, if any, it adopts, and a model that adopts none
is not thereby excluded.

**(v) Scope and exclusions.** Idealizations such as unmodeled self-force,
finite-size and tidal corrections, dispersion, dissipation, and quantum effects
are outside the framework unless the model's explicit equations include them;
matter concentrated in a distributional or lower-dimensional source, and
matter configurations whose fields fail to be smooth on the model domain, are
outside the stated smooth branch and require additional mathematics. The
adoption of a matter model is not a claim that it describes nature.

Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

This item fixes the unit and coordinate conventions used when the geometric
objects of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are read as a classical
gravitational model. It is a statement of conventions, not a physical law and
not a measurement.

**(a) Constants.** The framework uses the conversion constant $c>0$ with SI
dimension $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, the Newton constant $G_N>0$ with
dimension $\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$, and a signed
cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. Neither the
numerical value of $c$ nor that of $G_N$ is asserted by this item; the signs
and dimensions are part of the conventions. The coupling constant that appears
in the field law adopted later in the framework is

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$

with dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{2}$; consequently
$\kappa T$ has dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$ when the components $T_{ab}$ of a
stress-energy tensor in a $g$-orthonormal frame are measured in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.

**(b) Coordinates.** A smooth chart $(U,x)$ may be chosen in either of two
standard ways. In **length coordinates** one sets $x^0=ct$ with $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$
all measured in metres; then the metric components $g_{ab}$ are dimensionless,
$ds^2:=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has dimension $\mathrm m^2$, the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and curvature components and
the scalar curvature have dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. In **time coordinates**
one sets $x^0=t$ in seconds; then $g_{00}$ carries dimension
$\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ and the remaining components need not share a
dimension. Angular coordinates or mixed coordinates change individual
component dimensions by the Jacobians of the coordinate change; there is no
universal dimension attached to a single component of a tensor in a general
chart. The $g$-orthonormal frames of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]
are the frames in which components have the invariant dimensional readings
below.

**(c) Invariant quantities.** The following readings are part of the
conventions: $ds^2$ in $\mathrm m^2$; proper time $\tau$ in seconds;
four-velocity components $U^a=dx^a/d\tau$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$;
$g$-orthonormal components $T_{ab}$ of a stress-energy tensor in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; energy densities $T_{ab}n^an^b$ for unit timelike
$n$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; the cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ in
$\mathrm m^{-2}$; and the curvature components $R^a{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$
and $R$ in $\mathrm m^{-2}$.

**(d) Natural units.** The cited treatments frequently set $c=1$ and
sometimes $G_N=1$, equating units of length and time and, in the second case,
of mass and length. Such a choice is a shorthand for the conventions of
parts (a)-(c): a dimensionful result obtained in natural units must have the
factors of $c$ (and of $G_N$) restored before it is compared with an SI
quantity, and statements in this framework are stated with those factors
present. Natural-unit forms of equations are read as the corresponding SI forms
with the constants restored; the numerical value $c=1$ in one coordinate is
the coordinate statement $x^0=x^1$ in length coordinates for a null ray, not a
change of the physical constant.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) with metric-selected connection
$\nabla$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]), whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]; that theorem also
extends $\nabla$ to a derivative on tensor fields commuting with contractions
and annihilating $g$ and $g^{-1}$. Let $U\subseteq M$ be open and let
$X,Y,Z$ be smooth vector fields on $U$; brackets are those of
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]], and contractions those of
[[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]].

**(a) The curvature operator.** The **curvature operator** of $\nabla$ is the
assignment

$$R(X,Y)Z:=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z .$$

The right-hand side is a smooth vector field on $U$: $\nabla_YZ$ is smooth
because $\nabla$ is an affine connection
([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]), $[X,Y]$ is smooth, and
$\nabla_X(\cdot)$ and $\nabla_{[X,Y]}(\cdot)$ preserve smoothness. The
assignment is defined for the given smooth fields; that its value at a point
depends only on the values of $X,Y,Z$ at that point, so that $R$ is a smooth
tensor field of type $(1,3)$, is the content of
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (a), and
likewise the algebraic symmetries used below are proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]].

**(b) Component functions.** Let $(V,x)$ be a smooth chart of $M$ and let
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ be the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in this chart,
characterized by $\nabla_{\partial_b}\partial_c=\sum_a\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\partial_a$
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]); the coordinate fields
commute, so $\nabla_{\partial_c}\partial_d$ and $\nabla_{\partial_d}\partial_c$
are obtained from the same symbols. The **components** of the curvature in the
chart are the smooth functions $R^a{}_{bcd}$ on $V$ defined by

$$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=\sum_a R^a{}_{bcd}\,\partial_a .$$

The first index is the output slot, the second is the differentiated slot and
the last two are the two directions of the loop; indices are $a,b,c,d=0,1,2,3$
and the Einstein summation convention of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] applies.

**(c) Lowered tensor, Ricci tensor, scalar curvature, Einstein tensor.** On
the chart domain define, using the inverse metric
$g^{ab}$ of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

$$R_{abcd}:=\sum_e g_{ae}R^e{}_{bcd},\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{bd}:=\sum_{a,c}g^{ac}R_{abcd},\qquad S:=\sum_{b,d}g^{bd}\operatorname{Ric}_{bd},\qquad G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 S\,g_{ab}.$$

The fields $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$ and $G_{ab}$ are called
the **Riemann tensor with lowered indices**, the **Ricci tensor**, the
**scalar curvature** and the **Einstein tensor** of the metric-selected
connection. That $R_{abcd}$ are the components of a smooth $(0,4)$-tensor
field and that $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are the components of a smooth
symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field, so that the contractions above are
basis-independent and do not depend on the chart, is proved in
[[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] clauses (a)-(d); the Ricci symmetry
is part of that statement.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the matter-content
assumptions of the framework, the following rules by which ideal clocks, test
bodies and light couple to the metric $g$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].

**(i) Ideal clocks.** An **ideal clock** is an idealized physical device
carried along a future timelike worldline ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]])
whose readings are assumed to reproduce the proper time of that worldline:
the difference of two readings taken at two events of the worldline is the
proper-time increment between those events as defined by the metric, and it is
independent of the construction of the clock. Two ideal clocks moving along
the same worldline differ only by an additive constant (their choice of zero);
different worldlines generally accrue different proper times between the same
pair of events. The physical constant $c$ and the unit of duration are those
of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(ii) Free fall of massive test bodies.** A **test body** is an uncharged
idealized body whose internal structure is small compared with the scale over
which the geometry of the model varies and whose gravitational self-field is
negligible within the model. An **ideal freely falling massive test body** is
assumed to have a worldline that is a future timelike geodesic of the
metric-selected connection ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]), traversed with physical
four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$ satisfying
$g_{\gamma(\tau)}(U,U)=-c^2$; proper time is an affine parameter of the
worldline ([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). The
worldline is determined by the event at which the body is released together
with its four-velocity there, by the uniqueness of the geodesic initial-value
problem ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]); no force, charge, or
rest mass of the body enters this rule.

**(iii) Light rays.** In the geometric-optics approximation an **ideal light
ray** propagating in the model is assumed to be a future null geodesic of the
metric-selected connection
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]). A null worldline carries no proper
time and no four-velocity in the sense of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; within the approximation the
propagation of an ideal ray is independent of its frequency, and only the
ray's direction in the tangent space is fixed, not a scale along it.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** The three rules are adopted in the test-field
regime of the smooth classical model: the clocks, bodies and rays do not
back-react on the geometry, and the geometry varies smoothly on the scales
relevant to them. Configurations requiring the body's own gravitational field,
radiation reaction, an electromagnetic or other self-force, finite-size or
tidal couplings beyond the test-body idealization, non-geometric-optics
propagation, dispersion or dissipation of light, or quantum effects are
outside these assumptions and require additional model content. The
assumptions do not assert that any real clock, body or light ray is exactly
ideal, nor do they attach measured readings to any model.

Let a model of the classical gravitational framework be specified by a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ with its
metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and assume the
clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$U_0\in T_pM$ be a future timelike unit vector,
$g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

Suppose $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two ideal freely falling massive test bodies of
the model that are released at the event $p$ with physical four-velocity $U_0$:
their worldlines $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ pass through $p$ and their
four-vectors there equal $U_0$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be their proper
times, with origins chosen so that $\gamma_1(0)=\gamma_2(0)=p$. Then
$\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ coincide wherever both are defined:

$$\gamma_1(\tau)=\gamma_2(\tau)\qquad\text{for every }\tau\text{ in the common domain}.$$

and each is the maximal timelike geodesic through $(p,U_0)$. In particular the
worldline of an ideal freely falling massive test body is determined by the
release event and the initial four-velocity alone; parameters that distinguish
the two bodies, such as their rest masses, do not enter.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the derivative conditions below are imposed on the
  relative interval $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$ and are
  one-sided at $t_0$. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ is $C^1$, and the right tangent
  at $s_{i-1}$ and the left tangent at $s_i$ exist for every $i$. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. Existence of the one-sided
  tangents implies continuity of $\gamma$ at the corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the velocity derivation of
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] translated to the parameter
value $t$. In a chart around $\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** A **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The future timelike hypothesis
on the one-sided tangents makes the one-sided limits of $h_i$ at $s_{i-1}$ and
$s_i$ strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
$\tau(s):=\tau(s)-\tau(s_0)$ for the increment over the compact subinterval
bounded by $s_0$ and $s$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$c>0$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

1. **Well-definedness and additivity of proper time.** Let
   $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike worldline
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then the sum defining
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)$ is the same for every admissible partition of $[a,b]$; it
   is written $\frac1c\int_a^b h$, where $h$ is the piecewise-defined
   proper-time density. For $a<c<b$,
   $\tau(b)-\tau(a)=\bigl(\tau(c)-\tau(a)\bigr)+\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(c)\bigr)$.
   If $a<b$, the increment is strictly positive.

2. **Reparametrization invariance.** Let $\varphi:[a',b']\to[a,b]$ be $C^1$ with
   $\varphi'\neq0$ everywhere (so $\varphi$ is strictly monotone), and let
   $\tilde\gamma:=\gamma\circ\varphi$. Then $\tilde\gamma$ is a
   piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike worldline and
   $\tilde\tau(b')-\tilde\tau(a')=\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(a)\bigr)$ if $\varphi'>0$,
   while $\tilde\tau(b')-\tilde\tau(a')=-\bigl(\tau(b)-\tau(a)\bigr)$ if
   $\varphi'<0$.

3. **Proper-time function and four-velocity.** Let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a
   $C^1$ future timelike worldline on an interval with nonempty interior and
   let $\tau$ be its proper-time function based at $t_0\in I$
   ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]). Then $\tau$ is $C^1$ on
   $I$ with
   $$\tau'(t)=\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}>0,$$
   so $\tau$ is strictly increasing, and at every $t\in I$ the velocity,
   proper-time density and four-velocity satisfy
   $\gamma'(t)=\tau'(t)\,U(t)$ and $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$. If
   $\tau$ is strictly increasing on $I$ with image $J$, then the
   reparametrized curve $\gamma_\tau:=\gamma\circ(\tau|_I)^{-1}$ is a $C^1$
   future timelike worldline on $J$ with
   $$\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)=U\bigl(\tau^{-1}(\sigma)\bigr),\qquad g\bigl(\gamma_\tau'(\sigma),\gamma_\tau'(\sigma)\bigr)=-c^2 .$$
   The same formulas hold piece by piece for a piecewise-$C^1$ future
   timelike worldline, on each open piece.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with its inertial chart $x$,
and let $\nabla$ be its metric-selected connection, whose existence and
uniqueness are supplied by
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $c>0$ be a
real parameter.

**(a) Vanishing connection.** In the inertial chart all Christoffel symbols
of $\nabla$ vanish identically:

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}\equiv0\qquad(a,b,c=0,1,2,3).$$

**(b) Vanishing curvature.** The curvature operator of $\nabla$ vanishes
identically, $R\equiv0$; consequently the curvature components, the Ricci
tensor, the scalar curvature and the Einstein tensor vanish identically,

$$R^a{}_{bcd}\equiv0,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_{ab}\equiv0,\qquad S\equiv0,\qquad G_{ab}\equiv0 .$$

**(c) Translation Killing fields.** Each coordinate field $\partial_a$ is a
Killing field of $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-killing-field]]); in particular the time
orientation field $N=\partial_0$ is a unit timelike Killing field.

**(d) Straight geodesics.** A smooth curve $\gamma:I\to M$ on an interval
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ with nonempty interior
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]) is a geodesic of $\nabla$ if and
only if there are $x_0,v\in\mathbb R^4$ such that

$$x\bigl(\gamma(s)\bigr)=x_0+s\,v\qquad(s\in I).$$

For such a geodesic the speed is constant,
$g(\gamma',\gamma')=\eta(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2$; the maximal
geodesic with $x(\gamma(0))=x_0$ and $x(\gamma)'(0)=v$ has domain
$\mathbb R$. If $\eta(v,v)<0$ and $v^0>0$, the geodesic is a future timelike
worldline
([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]) and the parameter
$\tau(s):=\sqrt{-\eta(v,v)}\,(s-s_0)/c$ is proper time up to an additive
constant, with $d\gamma/d\tau$ the physical four-velocity
$U$, $g(U,U)=-c^2$
([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]] clause 3).

**(e) Inertial-chart velocity reading.** Let $\gamma$ be a geodesic as in
(d) with $\eta(v,v)<0$, $v^0>0$, written in the inertial chart as
$x(\gamma(t))=(ct,\mathbf q(t))$ with $\mathbf q$ the spatial part and $t$
the parameter $t=x^0/c$. Then the coordinate velocity
$\mathbf w:=d\mathbf q/dt$ is the constant vector
$(cv^1,v^0,\dots)$-reading $\mathbf w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$, and
$|\mathbf w|<c$.

Let $M:=\mathbb R^4$ carry its standard smooth structure
([[def-smooth-manifold]]), and let
$x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3):M\to\mathbb R^4$ be the **identity chart**, $x(p)=p$;
it is a global chart of the maximal smooth atlas, and the coordinate
derivations $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3$ form a basis of
$T_pM$ at every $p\in M$
([[def-derivation-at-a-point-and-tangent-space]],
[[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). Write

$$\eta:=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$$

for the standard Lorentz form of inertia $(3,1,0)$ in this basis
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]).

**(a) The metric.** Define the covariant $2$-tensor field $g$ on $M$ by the
requirement that its components in the identity chart are the constants

$$g_{ab}:=\eta_{ab}\qquad(a,b=0,1,2,3),$$

that is, $g_p(\partial_a|_p,\partial_b|_p)=\eta_{ab}$ for every $p\in M$
([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] clause (a)). The component
functions are constant, hence $C^\infty$, so $g$ is a smooth symmetric
covariant $2$-tensor field; at every $p$ the form $g_p$ is nondegenerate with
inertia $(3,1,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (a) the
pair $(M,g)$ is therefore a smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$.

**(b) The inertial chart and frame.** The chart $x$ is called the **inertial
chart** of the flat model. In this chart the coordinate frame
$(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2,\partial_3)$ is a $g$-orthonormal frame at
every point, $g(\partial_a,\partial_b)=\eta_{ab}$; it is simultaneously a
coordinate frame and a **tetrad field** in the sense of
[[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], defined on all of $M$.

**(c) Time orientation and causal classification.** Define the smooth vector
field $N:=\partial_0$ on $M$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]). Since
$g_p(N_p,N_p)=\eta_{00}=-1<0$ for every $p$, the field $N$ is everywhere
timelike, so $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c)). For a nonzero tangent
vector $v=v^a\partial_a|_p$ the definitions of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] clause (c) and
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]] give

$$g_p(v,v)=-(v^0)^2+\sum_{i=1}^3(v^i)^2,\qquad g_p(v,N_p)=-v^0 .$$

so $v$ is **future-directed** exactly when $v^0>0$, and

- $v$ is future timelike $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2>\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is future null $\iff$ $v^0>0$ and $(v^0)^2=\sum_i(v^i)^2$;
- $v$ is spacelike $\iff$ $(v^0)^2<\sum_i(v^i)^2$;

consequently the future causal cone at every point is
$\{v\neq0: v^0\ge\sqrt{\sum_i(v^i)^2}\}$. These are the standard readings of
the Minkowski form in the inertial chart; the chain of equivalences is the
specialization of the causal classification to this pair $(g_p,N_p)$ and is
recorded here for later use.

**(d) Scope.** This item defines geometric data only: a manifold, a metric
field, a time orientation and a distinguished chart and frame. It makes no
claim about curvature, about any field equation, about which geometry a
physical model uses, or about nature; the physical reading of the data, the
dimensions of the coordinates and the numerical values or signs of physical
constants belong to the framework's unit conventions and postulates, which
are separate items. In particular no relation between the coordinate
functions $x^a$ and physical time or length measurements is asserted here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
$\nabla_Xg=0$, and the compatibility of $\nabla$ with the inverse metric
$g^{-1}$ follows; neither statement is part of this definition.

**(b) Torsion freedom.** The **torsion** of $\nabla$ is the tangent-valued
$2$-tensor $T(X,Y)=\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX-[X,Y]$ of
[[def-torsion-tensor-of-an-affine-connection]], with bracket as in
[[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]]. The connection is **torsion-free**
when $T(X,Y)=0$ for all smooth $X,Y$, that is, when
$\nabla_XY-\nabla_YX=[X,Y]$ identically.

**(c) Metric-selected connections.** A **metric-selected connection** for
$(M,g)$ is an affine connection on $M$ that is both torsion-free and
$g$-compatible. Equivalently, it is an element of the class

$$\operatorname{LC}(M,g):=\{\nabla:\nabla\text{ is an affine connection on }M,\ \nabla\text{ is torsion-free and }g\text{-compatible}\}.$$

The name records that the pair of conditions selects the connection out of all
affine connections; it is the pair of conditions imposed on the connection that
conventional general relativity uses, and the connection so selected is called
the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]],
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on the tensor bundles
of [[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]. Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Adopt one of the two presentations of the framework's field law, that is,
[[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]] or
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]], for a model with geometric data and matter
sector satisfying [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]. Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth
time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
and curvature tensors $R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, $S$,
$G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]), let $T$ be the model's smooth
symmetric stress-energy tensor field on the matter domain
([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]), let $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be the
constant parameter and $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ as in
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], and suppose the field law holds,

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }M .$$

**(a) Necessary conservation.** $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ on $M$. Consequently a
prescribed smooth symmetric $T$ with $\nabla^aT_{ab}\neq0$ at some point cannot
satisfy the field law for any metric on which $T$ is smooth.

**(b) Trace.** $g^{ab}T_{ab}$ satisfies $-S+4\Lambda=\kappa\,g^{ab}T_{ab}$.

**(c) Parameter variation.** If instead $\Lambda:M\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth
function and the field law $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds with
that function in place of a constant, then

$$\kappa\nabla^aT_{ab}=\partial_b\Lambda .$$

Thus a nonconstant $\Lambda$ in the equation is consistent only with a
nonconserved $T$; the constant-parameter assumption is not redundant.

**(d) A vacuum solution.** On $M=\mathbb R^4$ with the identity chart and the
flat metric $g_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ (a smooth Lorentzian metric
with time orientation $N=\partial_0$), the field law with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$
holds: $G=0$ and $S=0$ for the flat metric. With $T=0$ and $\Lambda\neq0$ it
fails, since $G+\Lambda g=\Lambda g\neq0$.

**(e) Energy conditions are additional assumptions.** Neither adopted
presentation of the field law contains a clause imposing any of the weak, null,
dominant or strong energy conditions of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]]; each of
the four conditions is available to a model only as a further assumption in the
sense of clause (iv) of [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], and the field
law (a)-(d) derives none of them.

**(f) Perfect-fluid rest-frame reading.** Let $(\varepsilon,p,n,T)$ be a
perfect-fluid model on its matter domain
([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]), and at $p$ let
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ be a $g_p$-orthonormal basis with $e_0=n_p$. Then
$T_{AB}=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,p,p,p)$ in that basis, and at $p$

$$T\ \text{satisfies WEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies NEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+p\ge0,\qquad T\ \text{satisfies DEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon\ge|p|,$$

$$T\ \text{satisfies SEC}\Longleftrightarrow\varepsilon+3p\ge0\ \text{and}\ \varepsilon+p\ge0 .$$

In particular a model with $\varepsilon>0$ and $p=-\varepsilon$ satisfies the
NEC, WEC and DEC and violates the SEC; the inequality signs here are those of
the strict-timelike convention of [[def-gr-energy-conditions]], under which
continuity extensions to the causal cone are not assumed.

Adopt the postulates [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]] of the classical gravitational
framework, and let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented Lorentzian
four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and curvature
$R$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). All statements below
are deductions within the model so specified; they assert nothing about
nature.

**(a) Free-fall congruences.** A **free-fall congruence** of the model is a
smooth map $\gamma:(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\times I\to M$, with
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval with nonempty interior, such that for every
$r$ the curve $\gamma_r:=\gamma(\cdot,r)$ is a future timelike geodesic
parametrized by proper time: with $U_r:=\partial_s\gamma$,
$$g(U_r,U_r)=-c^2,\qquad \nabla_{U_r}U_r=0 .$$
By clause (ii) of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], each $\gamma_r$ is
a worldline the model assigns to an ideal freely falling massive test body
with the corresponding release data, and conversely every such worldline
arises this way.

**(b) Deviation equation (model deduction).** Let $\gamma$ be a free-fall
congruence and set $J:=\partial_r\gamma$. Then, along each $\gamma_r$, the
separation field satisfies
$$D_s^2J=R(U_r,J)U_r,$$
where $D_s$ is the covariant derivative along $\gamma_r$. In particular the
relative four-acceleration of nearby free-fall worldlines of the model is
exactly the curvature term: it is $\mathbb R$-linear in $J$, vanishes when
$J=0$, is a tensorial (frame- and coordinate-independent) linear map at each
event, and contains no rest mass, charge or internal-structure parameter of
the bodies.

**(c) Flat comparison and the vanishing criterion.** If the curvature
vanishes on an open subset $O\subseteq M$, then every free-fall congruence
with worldlines in $O$ has $D_s^2J=0$ there: the model predicts no tidal
relative acceleration of freely falling test bodies in that region.
Conversely, if at an event $q$ the operator $J\mapsto R(U,J)U$ vanishes for
every future timelike $U$ and every $J\in T_qM$, then $R_q=0$; hence within
the model the tidal response of all free-fall congruences detects exactly the
curvature, and $R$ is the model's complete tidal field at every event.

**Status.** Clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the stated
postulates and the cited mathematics. No observation, apparatus, measured
input or statistical inference is used; the item contains no empirical
premises, and the word "tidal" denotes the curvature term in the model's
deviation equation, not a measured force on any particular body.

derivations.claim: (The model and its field law.) By [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] clauses (a)-(c), $(M,g,N)$ is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold without boundary; by [A1] it satisfies the spacetime postulate, and $T=0$ is a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on the matter domain $M$. By [L1], $G_{ab}\equiv0$; with $\Lambda=0$ and $T=0$, $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=0=\kappa T_{ab}$ holds identically, and $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ trivially, so the prescription is admissible by [A1] and the field law holds by [A2]; this is also the flat vacuum solution of [L2]. This proves (a).

(Free fall and clock readings.) Let $p,U_0$ be as in (b), and write $U_0=c v$ with $\eta(v,v)=-1$, $v^0>0$; the normalization is possible by [[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] clause (c). By [A3] the worldline is the future timelike geodesic through $(p,U_0)$ with proper time as affine parameter, and by [A3] it is determined by $(p,U_0)$. By [L1] it is the straight line $x(\gamma(s))=x_0+sv$. With proper-time parametrization $\tau=s/c$ (the normalization $\lambda=1$ of [L1]), this is $x(\gamma(\tau))=x_0+c\tau v$; the coordinate velocity is the constant $w=(c/v^0)(v^1,v^2,v^3)$ with $|w|<c$ by [L1]. Finally, the ideal clock reads proper time by [A3], and from the parametrization $t=x^0/c$ along the line, $t-t_0=v^0\tau$; since $|w|^2/c^2=1-1/(v^0)^2$ by [L1] clause (e), $\sqrt{1-|w|^2/c^2}=1/v^0$ and hence $\Delta\tau=(1/v^0)(t_1-t_0)=\sqrt{1-|w|^2/c^2}(t_1-t_0)$. This proves (b).
(No tidal response.) The curvature vanishes identically by [L1], so by [L3] every free-fall congruence satisfies $D_\tau^2J=0$. This proves (c).

(Conclusion and status.) Steps 1.1-1.3 establish (a)-(c) as consequences of the adopted postulates and the cited mathematics, using no observation, apparatus or measured input; clause (d) records that the model is one solution among many and carries no empirical assertion, in particular no claim that the vacuum or the flat topology is realized in nature.

boundaries.reason: The model M is a nonempty four-manifold and the vacuum prescription T = 0 is a global field; no empty family or sum arises.

boundaries.evidence: statement clause (a) takes Λ = 0 and T = 0 and verifies G_ab = 0 identically by the vanishing curvature of the flat model; the zero parameter cases of the field law are the content of the model.

boundaries.reason: The dimension is four and no one-parameter specialization of the field law is asserted.

boundaries.evidence: statement clause (b) parametrizes worldlines by proper time using g(U0,U0) = -c², so the null and zero-velocity degenerate cases are excluded from the free-fall clause by hypothesis rather than silently assumed.
statement clause (b) integrates the clock reading between two coordinate times t0 < t1 and uses the maximal geodesic defined on all of ℝ, so both time endpoints are covered.

boundaries.reason: The event p and the four-velocity U0 are given data; the worldline is determined by them, and no selection occurs in the deduction.
The item asserts a conditional model statement and identities, not an equivalence.
No converse (for example that every vacuum solution is the flat model) is asserted; clause (d) explicitly states that other solutions are not excluded.

citations.quote:
Adopt as the field law of the direct-equation presentation of the classical
gravitational framework, for models satisfying
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]], the following statement.

**(i) The equation.** Let $(M,g,N)$ be the model's smooth time-oriented
Lorentzian four-manifold with metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]) and let
$G_{ab}=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12Sg_{ab}$ be the Einstein tensor of that
connection ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$T$ be the model's stress-energy tensor field on its matter domain
$U\subseteq M$ ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]]) and let
$\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ be a constant parameter with dimension
$\mathrm m^{-2}$ and $G_N>0$, $c>0$ the constants of
[[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Adopt

$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}\,T_{ab}\qquad\text{on }U$$

as the field law of the model. Writing
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ and $T_{ab}=g_{ac}g_{bd}T^{cd}$ for the lowered tensor,
the equation reads $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$

**(ii) Matter content.** The equation constrains the metric and the matter of
the model jointly. A model specifies its matter sector as in
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]: a scalar-field model with its action
and stress-energy tensor ([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]), or a dust or perfect-fluid model with prescribed
stress-energy tensor and matter equations. The consistency condition that
every solution must satisfy, $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$, is not adopted separately; it
is a consequence of the equation and of the contracted second Bianchi identity
and is derived in [[pthm-gr-einstein-consistency-and-energy-conditions]].

**(iii) Alternative presentation.** The action formulation of the same field
law is adopted separately in [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]. A
model adopts exactly one of the two presentations. They are alternative
presentations of one classical field law: the action-to-equation theorem of
this page identifies the equation obtained from stationarity of the total
action with the equation displayed in clause (i), and the direct presentation
is not an additional premise of an action-formulated model.

**(iv) Status and scope.** The equation is an adopted law of the model. It is
not derived from mathematical symmetry, from the equivalence principle, or
from observation; covariance and correspondence arguments motivate but do not
prove it. No numerical value of $c$, $G_N$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted, and no
claim is made that any particular metric or matter configuration solves the
equation or describes nature. The smooth-branch exclusions of
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] apply: distributional or
lower-dimensional sources, boundaries with junction conditions, and non-smooth
fields are outside this formulation. Comparisons of a model's predictions with
data test the combined model — geometry, matter content and this law — and
agreement is evidence about that combination, not a proof of the postulate.

Let $(M,g_\eta,N_\eta)$ be the flat model of
[[def-gr-minkowski-model-and-inertial-chart]] with inertial chart $x$ and
constant components $\eta_{ab}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, let
$\Omega\subseteq M$ be a nonempty open set identified with its chart image,
and let $c>0$ and $G_N>0$ be real parameters; put
$\kappa:=8\pi G_N/c^4$ as in the framework's convention. All components below
are taken in the inertial chart, and $\partial_a$ are the chart derivatives.

**(a) Structural data.** A tuple $(\Omega,K,L,C,\varepsilon_0,\varphi,r)$ is
**stationary weak-field data** when

- $K\subseteq\Omega$ is a compact set, $L>0$, $C>0$ and
  $\varepsilon_0>0$ are constants;
- $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth dimensionless function and
  $r=(r_{ab})$ is a family of component functions
  $r_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)$, defined for $\varepsilon\in(-\varepsilon_1,\varepsilon_1)$
  and $p\in\Omega$ for some $\varepsilon_1>\varepsilon_0$ and smooth in
  $(\varepsilon,p)$ ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]);
- for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$ the component field

$$g_{ab}(\varepsilon,p)=\begin{cases}-(1+2\varepsilon\varphi(p))+r_{00}(\varepsilon,p),&a=b=0,\\[2pt] r_{0i}(\varepsilon,p),&\{a,b\}=\{0,i\},\\[2pt] (1-2\varepsilon\varphi(p))\,\delta_{ij}+r_{ij}(\varepsilon,p),&a=i,\ b=j,\end{cases}$$

  is the component field of a smooth Lorentzian metric $g(\varepsilon)$ on
  $\Omega$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]);
- **(stationarity)** $\partial_0\varphi=0$ and $\partial_0r_{ab}=0$ on
  $\Omega$ for all $a,b$ and all $\varepsilon$, so that
  $\partial_0g_{ab}(\varepsilon,\cdot)=0$;
- **(bounds)** for every multiindex $\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le2$ and every
  $p\in K$,

$$|\partial^\alpha\varphi(p)|\le\frac{C}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{00}(\varepsilon,p)|+|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}(\varepsilon,p)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^2}{L^{|\alpha|}},\qquad |\partial^\alpha r_{0i}(\varepsilon,p)|\le\frac{C\varepsilon^{3/2}}{L^{|\alpha|}} .$$

  (Here $|\partial^\alpha r_{ij}|$ stands for the maximum over $i,j$ and
  $|\partial^\alpha r_{0i}|$ for the maximum over $i$.)

**(b) Derived data.** For stationary weak-field data define the
**potential**

$$\Phi:=\varepsilon c^2\varphi\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

a smooth stationary function of dimension $\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ in
the framework's unit conventions. The symmetric component family
$g(\varepsilon)-\eta$ is the **perturbation of the family**.

**(c) Einstein families.** Stationary weak-field data form an **Einstein
family with coupling $\kappa$** when for every $0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0$
there is a smooth symmetric component field $T_{ab}(\varepsilon,\cdot)$ on
$\Omega$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]) satisfying

$$G_{ab}\bigl(g(\varepsilon)\bigr)=\kappa\,T_{ab}(\varepsilon)\qquad\text{on }\Omega,$$

where $G$ is the Einstein tensor of the metric-selected connection of
$g(\varepsilon)$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). In that case define the
**density read from the time-time component**

$$\rho_\varepsilon:=\frac{T_{00}(\varepsilon)}{c^2}\qquad\text{on }\Omega .$$

**(d) Scope.** This item fixes a class of metric families and the vocabulary
of the weak-field bridge: the component form, the stationarity of the data,
the derivative bounds, the potential, and the equation that upgrades the
data to an Einstein family. It asserts that no family exists, that
$\partial_0$ is a Killing field or timelike, that the inverse metrics are
uniformly bounded or that the density is positive; those are consequences
proved separately where they are used. The family is an explicit
input-family hypothesis: neither its existence for prescribed Newtonian
initial data nor its construction from other data is claimed. The physical
reading of the components, of $G_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab}$, of $\Phi$ and of
$\rho_\varepsilon$ belongs to the framework's postulates and unit
conventions, which are separate items.

This item fixes the unit and coordinate conventions used when the geometric
objects of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]] and the tensor fields of
[[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]] are read as a classical
gravitational model. It is a statement of conventions, not a physical law and
not a measurement.

**(a) Constants.** The framework uses the conversion constant $c>0$ with SI
dimension $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$, the Newton constant $G_N>0$ with
dimension $\mathrm m^3\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$, and a signed
cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ with dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. Neither the
numerical value of $c$ nor that of $G_N$ is asserted by this item; the signs
and dimensions are part of the conventions. The coupling constant that appears
in the field law adopted later in the framework is

$$\kappa:=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4},$$

with dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm s^{2}$; consequently
$\kappa T$ has dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$ when the components $T_{ab}$ of a
stress-energy tensor in a $g$-orthonormal frame are measured in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}=\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm m^{-1}\mathrm s^{-2}$.

**(b) Coordinates.** A smooth chart $(U,x)$ may be chosen in either of two
standard ways. In **length coordinates** one sets $x^0=ct$ with $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$
all measured in metres; then the metric components $g_{ab}$ are dimensionless,
$ds^2:=g_{ab}dx^adx^b$ has dimension $\mathrm m^2$, the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and curvature components and
the scalar curvature have dimension $\mathrm m^{-2}$. In **time coordinates**
one sets $x^0=t$ in seconds; then $g_{00}$ carries dimension
$\mathrm m^2\,\mathrm s^{-2}$ and the remaining components need not share a
dimension. Angular coordinates or mixed coordinates change individual
component dimensions by the Jacobians of the coordinate change; there is no
universal dimension attached to a single component of a tensor in a general
chart. The $g$-orthonormal frames of [[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]
are the frames in which components have the invariant dimensional readings
below.

**(c) Invariant quantities.** The following readings are part of the
conventions: $ds^2$ in $\mathrm m^2$; proper time $\tau$ in seconds;
four-velocity components $U^a=dx^a/d\tau$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$;
$g$-orthonormal components $T_{ab}$ of a stress-energy tensor in
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; energy densities $T_{ab}n^an^b$ for unit timelike
$n$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$; the cosmological parameter $\Lambda$ in
$\mathrm m^{-2}$; and the curvature components $R^a{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$
and $R$ in $\mathrm m^{-2}$.

**(d) Natural units.** The cited treatments frequently set $c=1$ and
sometimes $G_N=1$, equating units of length and time and, in the second case,
of mass and length. Such a choice is a shorthand for the conventions of
parts (a)-(c): a dimensionful result obtained in natural units must have the
factors of $c$ (and of $G_N$) restored before it is compared with an SI
quantity, and statements in this framework are stated with those factors
present. Natural-unit forms of equations are read as the corresponding SI forms
with the constants restored; the numerical value $c=1$ in one coordinate is
the coordinate statement $x^0=x^1$ in length coordinates for a null ray, not a
change of the physical constant.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the classical gravitational framework, in
addition to [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]] and the matter-content
assumptions of the framework, the following rules by which ideal clocks, test
bodies and light couple to the metric $g$ of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]].

**(i) Ideal clocks.** An **ideal clock** is an idealized physical device
carried along a future timelike worldline ([[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]])
whose readings are assumed to reproduce the proper time of that worldline:
the difference of two readings taken at two events of the worldline is the
proper-time increment between those events as defined by the metric, and it is
independent of the construction of the clock. Two ideal clocks moving along
the same worldline differ only by an additive constant (their choice of zero);
different worldlines generally accrue different proper times between the same
pair of events. The physical constant $c$ and the unit of duration are those
of [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]].

**(ii) Free fall of massive test bodies.** A **test body** is an uncharged
idealized body whose internal structure is small compared with the scale over
which the geometry of the model varies and whose gravitational self-field is
negligible within the model. An **ideal freely falling massive test body** is
assumed to have a worldline that is a future timelike geodesic of the
metric-selected connection ([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]), traversed with physical
four-velocity $U=d\gamma/d\tau$ satisfying
$g_{\gamma(\tau)}(U,U)=-c^2$; proper time is an affine parameter of the
worldline ([[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]). The
worldline is determined by the event at which the body is released together
with its four-velocity there, by the uniqueness of the geodesic initial-value
problem ([[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]); no force, charge, or
rest mass of the body enters this rule.

**(iii) Light rays.** In the geometric-optics approximation an **ideal light
ray** propagating in the model is assumed to be a future null geodesic of the
metric-selected connection
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]],
[[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]). A null worldline carries no proper
time and no four-velocity in the sense of
[[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]; within the approximation the
propagation of an ideal ray is independent of its frequency, and only the
ray's direction in the tangent space is fixed, not a scale along it.

**(iv) Scope and exclusions.** The three rules are adopted in the test-field
regime of the smooth classical model: the clocks, bodies and rays do not
back-react on the geometry, and the geometry varies smoothly on the scales
relevant to them. Configurations requiring the body's own gravitational field,
radiation reaction, an electromagnetic or other self-force, finite-size or
tidal couplings beyond the test-body idealization, non-geometric-optics
propagation, dispersion or dissipation of light, or quantum effects are
outside these assumptions and require additional model content. The
assumptions do not assert that any real clock, body or light ray is exactly
ideal, nor do they attach measured readings to any model.

Let a model of the classical gravitational framework be specified by a
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ with its
metric-selected connection
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and assume the
clock, free-fall and light-ray assumptions of
[[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]. Let $p\in M$ and let
$U_0\in T_pM$ be a future timelike unit vector,
$g_p(U_0,U_0)=-c^2$ ([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]).

Suppose $B_1$ and $B_2$ are two ideal freely falling massive test bodies of
the model that are released at the event $p$ with physical four-velocity $U_0$:
their worldlines $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ pass through $p$ and their
four-vectors there equal $U_0$. Let $\tau_1$ and $\tau_2$ be their proper
times, with origins chosen so that $\gamma_1(0)=\gamma_2(0)=p$. Then
$\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ coincide wherever both are defined:

$$\gamma_1(\tau)=\gamma_2(\tau)\qquad\text{for every }\tau\text{ in the common domain}.$$

and each is the maximal timelike geodesic through $(p,U_0)$. In particular the
worldline of an ideal freely falling massive test body is determined by the
release event and the initial four-velocity alone; parameters that distinguish
the two bodies, such as their rest masses, do not enter.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $c>0$ be a fixed real constant.
All curves below take values in $M$; the physical reading of $c$, of a
worldline as the history of a clock or body, and of the parameter values as
times is not part of this definition and is adopted separately in the
postulates of the framework.

**(a) Regularity classes.** Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with
nonempty interior ([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be a map. A
**chart representative** of $\gamma$ is the map $x\circ\gamma$ for a smooth
chart $(U,x)$ of $M$ ([[def-smooth-manifold]]).

- For $k\in\mathbb N_0\cup\{\infty\}$ and an interior point $t_0\in I$, the map
  $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ at $t_0$** when there is a chart representative
  $x\circ\gamma$ defined near $t_0$ that is $C^k$ there in the componentwise
  Euclidean sense. This condition is independent of the chart: on the overlap
  of two chart representatives the transition map is smooth and the chain rule
  applies ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]],
  [[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]]). If $t_0\in I$ is an
  included endpoint of $I$, the derivative conditions below are imposed on the
  relative interval $I\cap(t_0-\delta,t_0+\delta)$ for some $\delta>0$ and are
  one-sided at $t_0$. The map $\gamma$ is **$C^k$ on $I$** when it is $C^k$ at
  every point of $I$.

- Let $b\in\mathbb R$ and $\varepsilon>0$. A curve
  $\gamma:(b-\varepsilon,b]\to M$ has **left tangent** $v\in T_{\gamma(b)}M$
  at $b$ when for one — equivalently every — chart $(U,x)$ around
  $\gamma(b)$, writing $v=\sum_{a=0}^{3}v^a\partial_a|_{\gamma(b)}$
  ([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]), the
  difference quotients satisfy
  $\bigl(x^a(\gamma(t))-x^a(\gamma(b))\bigr)/(t-b)\to v^a$ as $t\uparrow b$ for
  $a=0,1,2,3$. A **right tangent** at the left end of a curve is defined
  analogously with $t\downarrow b$. Chart independence is the one-sided
  chain-rule computation for the smooth transition maps
  ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]).

- A curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ with $a<b$ is **piecewise $C^1$** when there is a
  finite partition $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ such that for every $i$ the
  restriction of $\gamma$ to $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ is $C^1$, and the right tangent
  at $s_{i-1}$ and the left tangent at $s_i$ exist for every $i$. Such a
  partition is called **admissible** for $\gamma$. Existence of the one-sided
  tangents implies continuity of $\gamma$ at the corners; no agreement of the
  two one-sided tangents at a corner is required.

**(b) Velocity.** If $\gamma$ is $C^1$ at an interior point $t$, its
**velocity** $\gamma'(t)\in T_{\gamma(t)}M$ is the velocity derivation of
[[def-velocity-derivation-of-a-smooth-curve]] translated to the parameter
value $t$. In a chart around $\gamma(t)$ the velocity has the component
expression

$$\gamma'(t)=\sum_{a=0}^{3}\frac{d}{dt}\bigl(x^a\circ\gamma\bigr)(t)\,\partial_a|_{\gamma(t)},$$

the coordinate expression of the derivation
([[thm-coordinate-derivations-form-a-basis-of-the-tangent-space]]). At an
included endpoint of the domain, $\gamma'$ means the corresponding one-sided
tangent of clause (a).

**(c) Timelike worldlines.** A **$C^k$ future timelike worldline** is a $C^k$
curve $\gamma:I\to M$ whose velocity $\gamma'(t)$ is future timelike at every
$t\in I$, in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]
and [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]: $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t))<0$
and $g_{\gamma(t)}(\gamma'(t),N_{\gamma(t)})<0$. A **piecewise-$C^1$ future
timelike worldline** is a piecewise-$C^1$ curve $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ whose
velocity at every point of each open piece and whose one-sided tangents at the
two ends of each piece are future timelike; the definition is applied to a map
on an arbitrary interval $I$ with nonempty interior by requiring it on every
compact subinterval of $I$. A future timelike velocity is in particular
nonzero, so every future timelike worldline is regular.

**(d) Proper time and length.** Let $\gamma:[a,b]\to M$ be a piecewise-$C^1$
future timelike worldline and let $a=s_0<s_1<\cdots<s_m=b$ be an admissible
partition. On each open piece $(s_{i-1},s_i)$ the function

$$h_i(s):=\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(s)}\bigl(\gamma'(s),\gamma'(s)\bigr)}$$

is continuous and strictly positive: it is a finite sum of products of
continuous real functions in any chart around a point of the piece, as
$g_{ab}\circ\gamma$ and the components of $\gamma'$ are continuous
([[thm-componentwise-limits-and-continuity]],
[[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]], [[def-continuity-real]]), and the
square root is continuous on $(0,\infty)$ ([[def-rational-power]],
[[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]]). The future timelike hypothesis
on the one-sided tangents makes the one-sided limits of $h_i$ at $s_{i-1}$ and
$s_i$ strictly positive, and $h_i$ extends to a continuous function on
$[s_{i-1},s_i]$; hence it is Darboux integrable there
([[def-darboux-integral]], [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]). The
**proper-time increment** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is

$$\tau(b)-\tau(a):=\frac{1}{c}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\int_{s_{i-1}}^{s_i}h_i(s)\,ds,$$

and the **Lorentzian length** of $\gamma$ over $[a,b]$ is
$L_g(\gamma):=c\,(\tau(b)-\tau(a))$. For a base point $s_0\in I$ the
**proper-time function** $\tau:I\to\mathbb R$ of a future timelike worldline is
$\tau(s):=\tau(s)-\tau(s_0)$ for the increment over the compact subinterval
bounded by $s_0$ and $s$. That the increment is independent of the admissible
partition, so that $\tau$ is well defined, and that it is invariant under
increasing $C^1$ reparametrization are proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]]; the display is the
value for any admissible partition.

**(e) Four-velocity.** Let $\gamma$ be a piecewise-$C^1$ future timelike
worldline and let $t$ be a parameter value at which $\gamma$ is differentiable
(interior point of a piece, or an included endpoint with its one-sided
tangent). The **four-velocity** of $\gamma$ at $t$ is

$$U(t):=\frac{c\,\gamma'(t)}{\sqrt{-g_{\gamma(t)}\bigl(\gamma'(t),\gamma'(t)\bigr)}}\in T_{\gamma(t)}M .$$

By construction $g_{\gamma(t)}(U(t),U(t))=-c^2$, and
$\gamma'(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{-g(\gamma',\gamma')}/c\bigr)U(t)$ with a strictly
positive scalar factor. If $U$ is written as the derivative of $\gamma$ with
respect to proper time, $U=d\gamma/d\tau$, this is a statement proved in
[[lem-gr-proper-time-reparametrization-and-four-velocity]], not part of the
present definition.

**(f) Scope.** Proper time, length and four-velocity are defined only for
future timelike worldlines. A null or spacelike curve receives no proper time
and no four-velocity from this definition, and no limiting or distributional
extension of the square-root integrand to such curves is asserted. The
parametrization of a worldline is part of the data and is arbitrary in this
definition: no affine parameter, no geodesic equation, no completeness or
extendability of the domain, and no measurement or clock reading is assumed.
Null and spacelike regularity classes are not defined here beyond the general
$C^k$ and piecewise-$C^1$ notions of clause (a), which make no causal
requirement.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $\nabla$ be an affine connection
on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]). Smooth vector fields
are smooth sections of the tangent bundle
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]); as there, their use
rests on the canonical smooth structure of $TM$, which assumes the axiom
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]]. This is the only use of that
axiom in this definition.

**(a) Metric compatibility.** The connection $\nabla$ is **$g$-compatible**, or
**compatible with the metric** $g$, when for all smooth vector fields $X,Y,Z$ on
$M$ the identity of smooth functions

$$X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$$

holds on $M$. Here $g(Y,Z)$ is the smooth function $p\mapsto g_p(Y_p,Z_p)$ and
$X$ acts on functions as a derivation; the identity uses only the action of
$\nabla$ on vector fields and requires no extension of $\nabla$ to tensor
fields. When such an extension is available, this identity is the statement
